title: A Summer in Norway; with Notes on the Industries, Habits, Customs and Peculiarities of the People, the History and Institutions of the Country, Its Climate, Topography and Productions. Also, an Account of the Red-Deer, Reindeer and Elk
summary: John Dean Caton (1812–1895), a former Chief Justice of Illinois with a naturalist’s interest in deer, spent the summer of 1874 in Norway. He went up the coast by steamer to Trondhjem, Hammerfest, and the North Cape, visited Lapp reindeer herders near Tromsø, and came back south by carriole over the Dovrefjeld to Christiania, leaving by way of Stockholm. He writes of the people he met, farms, inns, and roads, and adds long passages on the history of Norway and on its red deer, reindeer, and elk.
